notes.text: Clayton Vernon told the owner he has a simplified version of Brad's working gas price model. Assumptions: no-arbitrage equates trading margins across the country; transmission costs rise with network congestion; wellhead supply is nearly perfectly price-elastic; burner-tip demand is nearly inelastic; storage is a perpetual call option.

Clayton said the model has 8 parameters to estimate at each major node. Least time-variant: storage injection/withdrawal costs, then wellhead-to-pipeline delivery costs. Intermediate: capacity-dependent pipeline transmission charges above shrinkage. Most time-variant: trading margins and storage option valuations.

Clayton said the 8 node parameters can be identified either from a short time series of the last 3 days' prices, or from point calibrations using only today's data, based on a node-based model of competition between pipelines.

Clayton Vernon told the owner he will write up the simplified gas price model in Scientific Word and present it to the owner at his earliest convenience. Message dated 1999-12-22, cc Vasant Shanbhogue.

notes.text: Anjam Ahmad announced (1999-12-22) a new UK power volatility curve generator, with curves down to EFA/monthly detail, marked to market up to 6 years out; beyond that, volatility decays to a long-term level.

Anjam said swaption traders can fit the first 5-6 years of the curve to market baseload swaption implied vols (typically 3-12 month swap tenors), then price EFA-slot swaptions consistently with the curve.
Anjam said the curves will be reset as the market moves, enabling mark-to-market for the volatility book, and may affect the daily VaR calculation.

notes.text: Robert Brooks (RBAC) wrote in a 1999-12-23 year-end letter to GPCM licensees that the number of GPCM licensees doubled to 10 during 1999.
Brooks said RBAC plans to convert GPCM from Office 97 to Office 2000 in 2000 and make sure it runs in the Windows 2000 environment.

Brooks listed planned 2000 GPCM features: more flexible transportation zone price curves for pipeline users, a capability for modeling future FT contracting, and an upgraded Database Comparison program with selectable automatic updates.

Brooks said RBAC will keep working with RDI on pipeline and storage infrastructure data, GASdat-GPCM interfaces, and optional database updates. Mike Farina and RDI were credited for GPCM data and GASdat improvements.

RBAC acquired gpcm.rbac.com and gpcm.net for a planned licensee website. Brooks said licensee interviews on enhancements would be conducted in the 30-60 days after the letter. Liam Leahy, Charles Carr, Richard Berman, Richard McBride were thanked for 1999 work.
